stories.headline: Guardians to open with Armstrong; Rays start Martinez in ALCS Game 4
stories.summary: Shawn Armstrong will be the opener for Cleveland and Tampa Bay will start Nick Martinez in Game 4 of the AL Championship Series on Friday night.
stories.body:
CLEVELAND -- Shawn Armstrong will be the opener for Cleveland and Tampa Bay will start Nick Martinez in Game 4 of the AL Championship Series on Friday night.

The Guardians have a 2-1 lead in the best-of-seven series after Petey Halpin's two-run homer propelled them to a 3-2 victory in Game 3 on Thursday afternoon.

Both teams waited to announce their pitching plans because of the weather. It is supposed to rain in Cleveland most of Friday, but there is a window between 8-11 p.m. ET that could allow them to get the game played.

The start time was also moved back two hours to 8 p.m. ET after the Milwaukee Brewers swept the Los Angeles Dodgers in the NL Championship Series Thursday night.

An ALCS game has not been postponed since 2019, when the New York Yankees hosted the Houston Astros.

This will be Armstrong's fifth appearance this postseason in what will be a bullpen game for Cleveland. The right-hander has allowed only one hit in 5⅓ innings with five strikeouts.

Armstrong thought his season was done in late July when he suffered a calf strain, but he returned during the final week of the regular season.

Armstrong was drafted by Cleveland in the 18th round in 2011 and made his big league debut four years later. He was traded to Seattle in 2017 and spent time with four other organizations, including Tampa Bay, before signing with Cleveland this season.

"I think I said it to [Erik] Sabrowski, whenever we were standing in the outfield in Game 2 in Tampa -- obviously I played here, I got drafted here, coming back here and being able to be in this situation is -- words can't describe it," Armstrong said before Thursday's game.

Martinez started Game 3 of the AL Division Series against the New York Yankees. He went 3⅔ innings, allowing two runs on five hits with a walk and three strikeouts. The right-hander went 15-6 during the regular season and was sixth in the AL with a 3.10 ERA. He was third in the AL with 26 starts where he allowed three runs or fewer.

"It's just like my starts throughout the year; it's going to be a dogfight going in, just to see how many outs I can get for this team, it's important," he said Thursday.

stories.headline: David Moyes on new contract talks at Everton: 'Bit of a lull'
stories.summary: David Moyes has said discussions over a new contract at the Hill Dickinson Stadium have gone quiet following news that Everton could be up for sale.
stories.body:
David Moyes has said discussions over a new contract at the Hill Dickinson Stadium have gone quiet following the news that Everton could be up for sale.

Everton's owners -- The Friedkin Group -- announced last week they were exploring the possibility of selling their controlling interest in the Merseyside outfit.

Toffees manager Moyes is in the final year of his deal and the Scot is not expecting imminent developments on fresh terms.

"There's been plenty of talks happening through the summer but maybe with the way things have gone at the moment, there's maybe been a bit of a lull, trying to get things in order," Moyes said at a news conference.

"But like I've said many times, it's not the most important thing for me. I just want to keep trying to drive Everton on and build them up, and see if we can continue to improve."

- Everton put up for sale by Friedkin Group

- 777 exec Wander, who led Everton bid, guilty of fraud; to repay $500M

Everton host Chelsea in the Premier League on Saturday.

Moyes said: "Anytime I've played Chelsea, it's always been a good game. It was always tough.

"But we will do our best. We're in quite a good place. We've been playing well ourselves."

stories.headline: NBA tells sportsbooks to stop certain bets, restrict parlays
stories.summary: The NBA is prohibiting certain bets this season, including a player prop parlay used in recent scandals, according to a league memo to sportsbook partners.
stories.body:
The NBA is prohibiting certain types of bets this season, including a player prop parlay used by gamblers in recent betting scandals, according to a league memo distributed to sportsbook partners Friday.

Bettors will not be able to include the under on the same player's statistics in parlays, in addition to other betting markets the league considers problematic, according to the memo, which was obtained by ESPN.

The league also directed its authorized gambling operators, including DraftKings and FanDuel, not to offer bets on the winner of the opening tip, players to miss specific shots and under bets on players who are expected to play fewer than 12 minutes in a specific game.

"There's a balance between ensuring that we are removing problematic bet types but also ensuring that we don't just move activity into the illegal market," NBA executive vice president Scott Kaufman-Ross told ESPN. "And where we landed right now, we think, is the right balance of those two objectives."

The NBA has the authority to restrict what partner sportsbooks offer through its agreements. The NBA estimates its partner sportsbooks account for upward of 99% of the U.S. betting market.

"The legalized sports betting industry is built on a foundation of dialogue and collaboration with our league partners and the states in which we operate," a FanDuel spokesperson said in a statement to ESPN. "We remain unwavering in our commitment to building a legal and regulated market that roots out abuses by those who seek to undermine fair competition and damage the integrity of the games we love."

Parlay bets on a single player's unders appeared in the federal cases involving NBA players Jontay Porter and Terry Rozier.

Porter admitted in court that he intentionally removed himself from games early to benefit bettors while he was on a two-way contract with the Toronto Raptors during the 2023-24 season.

In the criminal complaint, federal prosecutors said one of the bettors charged in the scheme placed an $80,000 parlay on the under on Porter's assists, rebounds, points, 3-pointers, steals and blocks for a March 2024 game between the Raptors and Sacramento Kings that would pay approximately $1.1 million. Porter left the game after playing only three minutes.

Federal prosecutors allege bettors took a similar approach a year earlier with parlays involving the under on Rozier's stats in a March 2023 game between the Charlotte Hornets and New Orleans Pelicans. The veteran guard, who was with the Hornets at the time, left after playing approximately nine minutes. Rozier has pleaded not guilty and denied wrongdoing.

Kaufman-Ross said the Porter and Rozier cases were factors in the decision to prohibit such parlays that were described as "low likelihood, high payout bets" in the memo. Sportsbooks also will be prohibited from offering alternate lines on unders with larger payouts.

"Seeing where we may have had issues in the past is one of the inputs to determining the types of things that we think could be problematic," Kaufman-Ross said.

After the scheme involving Porter was discovered, the NBA banned sportsbooks from taking under bets on players who are on two-way contracts.

Kaufman-Ross said that the league considered the entire betting landscape, including prediction markets, when deciding on the restrictions. The NBA has not announced any formal partnerships with prediction markets, and Kaufman-Ross acknowledges that without such agreements, enforcing its restrictions on prediction markets could be challenging.

A DraftKings spokesperson said some of the NBA's new restrictions are already reflected in the sportsbook's practices. DraftKings is the official odds provider for ESPN.

"DraftKings supports the NBA's efforts and is committed to continued collaboration with the league to maintain game integrity, including through appropriate limits on betting markets," the spokesperson said in a statement to ESPN. "DraftKings' Code of Responsible Engagement is fully aligned with the league's stance on the harassment of athletes, coaches or officials."

The league also distributed a memo to teams Friday, highlighting new integrity measures being put in place this season.

According to the memo, former NFL star and retired FBI agent Charles Tillman will lead in-person training on the league's sports betting rules. The league is also enhancing its in-house AI-based data monitoring platform designed to detect and investigate unusual betting activity on NBA games or events.

The memo stated that the NBA is also trying to better protect players, coaches and personnel from harassment by sports bettors by updating its fan code of conduct to highlight rules around harassment or threats by sports bettors.

The league has partnered with Social Protect, a third-party service provider that allows players to opt in to identify and delete harassing messages on social media, and it has also launched a new text-message-based hotline where harassment and threats can be securely reported.

ESPN's Shams Charania contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Fantasy hockey rankings: How high should Rangers goalies be ranked?
stories.summary: Connor McDavid and Macklin Celebrini lead, while Igor Shesterkin's injury shakes up the goalie rankings.
stories.body:
All that offseason prognostication goes out the door with the first in-season fantasy rankings of 2026-27. As always, these blend historical performance with current trajectory. Hot starts matter, but not nearly as much as what's still to come. These are go-forward rankings, built on the fantasy points yet to be scored.

The biggest shakeup comes from Broadway. With Igor Shesterkin out for the season with a knee injury, the rankings put Dylan Garand inside the top 100. But some of the bloom came off the rose Thursday, when Garand and Spencer Martin combined to allow seven goals to the New Jersey Devils. That's why Joonas Korpisalo, still projected out until mid-November, makes the cut as a stash for when Garand's hold on the crease loosens.

These rankings are based on expectations of fantasy points produced from Friday, Oct. 16, until the end of the season. Fantasy points are based on the ESPN Fantasy standard game (for skaters: goals = 2 points, assists = 1 point, shots and hits = 0.1 points, blocked shots and special-teams points = 0.5 points; for goaltenders: wins = 4 points, OT losses = 1 point, shutouts = 3 points, saves = 0.2 points, goals against = -2 points).

stories.headline: Harry Kane has talent for NFL - Jags kicker Cam Little
stories.summary: Cam Little is confident Harry Kane has the skill to become an NFL kicker.
stories.body:
LONDON -- Cam Little is confident Harry Kane has the skill to become an NFL kicker.

But the hard part for Kane, the Jacksonville Jaguars kicker said, would be shifting from star striker to bit player.

"I think the transition from soccer to football is so much more cultural than like the actual skill," Little said.

The England captain and Bayern Munich forward has mused over the years about one day kicking in the NFL. He recently floated the idea of combining his NFL goal with also joining an MLS team.

Who better to weigh in than Little? The soccer player-turned kicker, who remains a diehard Manchester United fan, booted a 57-yard field goal as time expired for the Jags to defeat the Philadelphia Eagles 19-17 last Sunday at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. He also holds the record for longest NFL field goal -- 68 yards.

"It's just so different," Little told The Associated Press of moving from being involved in a game for 90 minutes to being a kicker "sitting there on the sidelines the whole game.

"You're not going to get on the ball, and you don't have the same moxie, I guess, because he is a star striker for the team. So that moxie is just kind of put to the side. You've got to let everyone else do the big man's job, and then you're out there just to back everyone up basically."

As far as Kane's ability, "he's probably talented enough to do it ... His technique in soccer is so good. But it's just such a different mental, I'd say, challenge than soccer.

"It'd be like him taking five set pieces a day. And he's got to deliver on all five set pieces, or you didn't do your job for the day," Little said Thursday after practice at the team's accommodations north of London in Watford.

"So, it's just a lot different, but I don't think he doesn't have the talent level for it. I think he probably has the skill to do it."

Little and the Jaguars remained in London this week ahead of the game against the Houston Texans on Sunday at Wembley Stadium.

Little, a sixth-round draft pick from Arkansas in 2024, had missed an extra-point attempt -- after a high snap from fill-in long snapper DaVon Hamilton -- late in the fourth quarter against the Eagles. The miss had looked crucial because Philadelphia then took a 17-16 lead with just 8 seconds left -- before the improbable ending on Little's heroics.

"Missing a set piece or missing a wide-open goal, you see a lot of strikers do that, and they'll come back and put the game away," Little said at his post-game news conference while wearing a Man United jersey. "I've got to have short-term memory and be at my best when the best is required."

Little told AP that he'd be attending Fulham's home game against Hull at Craven Cottage on Saturday. Jaguars owner Shad Khan also owns the Premier League club.

Little, an Oklahoma native, played as a midfielder before switching to American football in high school. England and United great Wayne Rooney was his favorite player.

"Maybe one day I'll get to meet him or do a jersey swap with him. That's my goal," he said. "I've never been to Manchester. Only London, but I'm hoping to make it there this offseason."

stories.headline: Shakhtar's Champions League win vs. AEK was more than just a game
stories.summary: Shakhtar Donetsk haven't played at home since 2014 due to the war, and this season, their Champions League home games are at Chelsea's Stamford Bridge. Wednesday's win was a reminder of how absurd their situation is.
stories.body:
LONDON -- Take a step back and revel in the absurdity for a minute. Shakhtar Donetsk, a Ukrainian team from the Russian-speaking part of the country, are playing a Greek team, AEK Athens, in London, at Chelsea's Stamford Bridge. Technically, it's a "home game," but that concept has become rather meaningless.

Shakhtar haven't played at their home, the Donbas Arena, since May 2014, some 650 weeks ago. They turn up wherever someone will host them: Odessa, Kyiv, Kharkiv and Lviv for Ukrainian league games; Warsaw, Hamburg, Gelsenkirchen, Krakow, Ljubljana and now London for matches in European competition. Why? Because their opponents can't (or won't) travel to Ukraine, where none of the civilian airports are open, air raid sirens go off a dozen times a day, and where drones and bombs can't be trusted to distinguish between a military captain and the captain of a soccer team.

It's pretty obvious that in those circumstances, you're more than a club -- you're a symbol of defiance, an attempt to maintain some sort of normality in the face of a war that has taken more than half a million lives and displaced tens of millions more.

"We are playing for people from Ukraine all over the world," sporting director Dario Srna said. "Everywhere we've gone, they've come [to see us]. We represent Ukraine in the center of the world: we're not just playing for us. [We are] a Ukrainian team, we are not just Shakhtar."

But, of course, nothing is normal. Everything is messed up, and their mere presence in the Champions League constitutes a political dimension.

Wednesday night, Shakhtar were at Stamford Bridge, the home of Chelsea. Resourceful as ever, street vendors outside the ground hawked their off-brand scarves, except rather than "Cole Palmer," "João Pedro" and "John Terry," the names read "Pedrinho," "[Mykola] Matviyenko" and "[Valeriy] Bondar." Watching over them was a life-size cardboard cutout of Dwayne Johnson, aka The Rock, only his face was replaced by that of Ukrainian President Vladimir Zelenskyy.

Inside, visiting AEK fans -- who turned the Shed End into a two-tier wall of tifo, flags and noise -- outsing, if not outnumber, the "home" support.

Because yes, this is Shakhtar's home for the Champions League this season, a move made possible by the London club's failure to qualify for European competitions (and, probably, a need to rake in some extra rent on those empty weeknights). Ironically, Chelsea's previous owner, Roman Abramovich, was forced by the U.K. government to sell the club after the invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, because of his ties to Russian President Vladimir Putin. Abramovich holds passports from Portugal, Israel and Russia. His yachts are moored in Turkey.

Abramovich, whose mother is Ukrainian, is a complicated figure. So is Shakhtar's version of Abramovich, Rinat Akhmetov.

An ethnic Russian, but Donetsk-born and bred, Akhmetov's huge wealth from mining and energy bankrolled the club's rise to prominence prewar -- lest we forget, the likes of Willian and Fernandinho, Henrikh Mkiytaryan and Douglas Costa are all Shakhtar alums -- and keeps it alive and very much kicking today. Forbes estimates his wealth at nearly $8 billion and like most folks of that ilk, Akhmetov could easily have made different choices, decamping abroad. When the war broke out, he chose to stay, and that was not something to take for granted, given that he had previously clashed with Zelenskyy and, in the 2000s, served in parliament in the party of former pro-Russian Ukrainian President Viktor Yanukovych, whom he also backed financially.

Akhmetov broke with Yanukovych in 2014 and while his pro-Ukrainian words today are loud, his actions -- from staying in the country to tirelessly campaigning to his efforts with Shakhtar -- speak even louder.

"He can't leave Ukraine, not after seeing what he has seen," Srna says of Akhmetov. "It's impossible. He's devoted himself to this, helping the economy, helping the people. All while sleeping each night under bombs."

Many Ukrainians have no choice, which makes the actions of those who could be elsewhere all the more remarkable. It takes an unconventional type of person.

Most of Shakhtar's players are Brazilian -- lured by money, sure, but also the opportunity to showcase their talent. The coach, former Atletico Madrid and Barcelona standout Arda Turan, is Turkish. Even if you don't remember what he was like as a player, watching him prowl the technical area during the AEK game, fists clenched and eyes wild, you come to understand how this is the same guy who once got into an altercation with a pop star in an Istanbul hospital.

Srna himself is Croatian, but has been at the club -- first as a player then as sporting director -- for 23 years. He too could have left umpteen times and, in fact, he says he even turned down the chance to take over Barcelona's recruitment a decade ago.

"Ukraine and Shakhtar are in my blood," he says. "If I leave now, I couldn't live with myself."

In some ways, Srna has been here before. He was eight years old when civil war broke out in the former Yugoslavia in March 1991. The conflict that would rage for 4½ years, ripped apart communities along ethnic lines. Neighbors took up arms against neighbors. His own father woke up every day supplying baked goods for the military. If you've seen the ESPN 30 for 30 documentary "Once Brothers" about the relationship between Drazen Petrovic and Vlade Divac, well ... he lived it. Twice. Maybe that's why he soldiers on, numb to what he is experiencing.

"I have this feeling inside myself," he says. "It's a feeling I felt before [as a child experiencing war in Croatia]. But when you feel that pain and it comes back to you again, well, you're not going to have the same pain twice. I know this pain. I know this feeling ..."

Srna trails off as he searches for the right words of history -- the worst parts -- repeating itself with him in the middle of it. But then he flickers back with righteous anger.

"This is unbelievable, I can't explain it," he says. "Four-and-a-half years [this war has continued]. Bombing each other, destroying everything ... for what? For f---ing what? People die, families are destroyed, children are traumatized and grow up with psychological problems ..."

On this Wednesday night, even as Shakhtar emerge as 3-1 victors over AEK, you're reminded once again of the difficulties. The team were up at 6 a.m. on Thursday to catch a 10 o'clock flight on a plane they chartered from a budget airline taking them back to Rzeszow in Poland. They'll then board a bus back across the border into Ukraine, arriving -- best-case scenario -- at 9 p.m. local time. All this not knowing whether they'll have power and heat when they arrive, or whether they'll be making regular trips into the air raid shelter.

You want to end on a note of hope. Srna does his best to offer it, but he clearly isn't going to lie to you or to himself.

"We [Croatians] have more or less an OK relationship now with Serbia," he says. "Time [30 years have passed] is helping, generations change, it's different people. We take a step back and understand what was good, what was not good. We can't say all Serbian people are bad ... But in this moment, it's not possible to be friends with a Russian person. In time, maybe a few years, maybe many years, I don't know ... right now though, it's impossible."

Certainly more impossible than a club without a home in a country at war defying logic and competing in the Champions League against the likes of Real Madrid, who visit Stamford Bridge on Jan. 27.

One of the side effects of war is the normalization of the horrific and the absurd. Shakhtar's plight has, by necessity, normalized the absurd, in an effort to stave off the horrific.

stories.headline: Ranking Angel Reese and the top 15 players in the WNBA Finals
stories.summary: Which Valkyries and Dream players have played the best so far in the postseason heading into the WNBA Finals?
stories.byline: Michael Voepel and Alexa Philippou and Kendra Andrews and Kareem Copeland
stories.body:
Two teams. One title on the line.

The WNBA Finals open Saturday (3:30 p.m. ET) as the No. 2 seed Golden State Valkyries and No. 4 Atlanta Dream square off in a best-of-seven series. Both are seeking their first championship. Which players are most likely to help them finish on top?

ESPN has ranked the top players throughout the 2026 season. Now we update our list one final time to reflect the 15 players who have performed the best in the playoffs.

Rotations get shorter in the postseason, but with their incredible depth, it's likely no surprise the Valkyries added one more player in our rankings. But with three All-Stars on their roster, it's perhaps also no shock that the Dream dominated the top, with three of the first four players.

The rankings come with one asterisk: Dream guard Allisha Gray, when healthy, is easily one of the WNBA's best. But she sustained a hand injury in the first game of the semifinals and hasn't played since.

Gray made the cut after she said Thursday she was optimistic about playing in Game 1 at Chase Center in San Francisco.

Here are the best 15 players in the postseason, as ranked by Michael Voepel, Alexa Philippou, Kendra Andrews and Kareem Copeland.

1. Angel Reese, Atlanta Dream
Forward | 6-foot-3

Playoff stats: 18.0 PPG, 8.4 RPG, 2.0 APG

The 2024 No. 7 draft pick is playing the best ball of her career and was recently named the league's Defensive Player of the Year. In her first postseason, Reese is averaging 18.0 points, 8.4 rebounds, 2.2 blocks, 2.0 assists and 1.6 steals. The scoring and blocks have both increased and she's shooting 38.5% from beyond the arc. Reese's impact on both ends of the court is, arguably, the biggest reason the Dream are in the Finals for the first time since 2013. -- Copeland

2. Gabby Williams, Golden State Valkyries
Forward | 5-foot-11

Playoff stats: 22.7 PPG, 4.8 RPG, 4.0 APG

Williams' breakout offensive season has continued in the playoffs. She is the highest scorer remaining in the Finals, averaging nearly 23 points, eight more than her regular-season average. She is shooting 40.5% from 3 on 2.8 attempts (fourth in the playoffs, and the most among players in the Finals). After finishing second in Defensive Player of the Year voting, Williams' two-way play has the Valkyries in the Finals and within striking distance of winning a title. -- Andrews

3. Rhyne Howard, Atlanta Dream
Guard | 6-foot-2

Playoff stats: 19.2 PPG, 4.2 RPG, 3.4 APG

Howard has had an up-and-down playoffs. She didn't make more than a third of her shots from the field in any of the semifinal games, though she went 4-for-10 from deep in Game 3 to help the Dream close out the series. She still excels with her versatility, whether she's making 3s, getting downhill and drawing contact, facilitating for teammates or wreaking havoc on defense. -- Philippou

4. Jordin Canada, Atlanta Dream
Guard | 5-foot-6

Playoff stats: 19.2 PPG, 3.8 RPG, 8.8 APG

Canada, the No. 5 pick in the 2018 draft, won two WNBA titles in 2018 and 2020 with Seattle. She was a backup to Sue Bird then and didn't start any of those postseason games but played valuable minutes. Now she is in the driver's seat during these playoffs, averaging almost seven points more in the Dream's five postseason games than she did in the regular season. She has also been a defensive catalyst, averaging 2.2 steals. At 31, Canada is playing her best basketball at the best time. -- Voepel

5. Veronica Burton, Golden State Valkyries
Guard | 5-foot-9

Playoff stats: 9.5 PPG, 4.0 RPG, 4.0 APG

Burton hasn't had the most consistent postseason run, but she has delivered some of the Valkyries' biggest shots when they've needed a bucket the most. After not scoring late into Game 2 against Las Vegas in the semifinals, Burton hit a 28-foot 3-pointer to give the Valkyries the lead with about 90 seconds left. In the first round, she also hit a dagger shot against Dallas to help come back from being down 16 to win the game -- and the series. -- Andrews

6. Allisha Gray, Atlanta Dream
Guard | 6-foot

Playoff stats: 17.0 PPG, 1.7 RPG, 2.0 SPG (three games)

Gray was the Dream's top scorer in the regular season and in the first round of the playoffs but is lower on this list than she'd typically be because of her limited availability in the postseason. She went down with an injury to her left (shooting) hand in the first half of Game 1 of the semifinals and hasn't played since, though she was questionable going into Game 3. Gray disclosed this week that she underwent a minor procedure for the injury and is still considered day-to-day. She told reporters Thursday she was hopeful about her availability for Game 1. -- Philippou

7. Tiffany Hayes, Golden State Valkyries
Guard | 5-foot-10

Playoff stats: 13.3 PPG, 2.8 RPG, 2.3 APG

The 14-year veteran has provided the offensive punch off the bench that the Valkyries have needed. Her 13.3 points per game during the playoffs, after a 9.0 regular-season average, ranks No. 3 on a team known more for defense than offense. She dropped 21 points in a Game 1 win over the Wings in the opening round, then went for 18 in the Game 3 series clincher. Hayes scored 21 points in less than 17 minutes in the Game 2 semifinal against Las Vegas. -- Copeland

8. Kiah Stokes, Golden State Valkyries
Center | 6-foot-3

Playoff stats: 3.2 PPG, 9.5 RPG, 2.0 BPG

One of the ultimate "stats don't define her" players, Stokes' value is in how well she fills the exact role she's asked to play. Still, one stat stands out: She has averaged almost four more rebounds in the playoffs than the regular season. She is a textbook solid defender who benefited from guarding A'ja Wilson in practice during their five years in Las Vegas. While there, Stokes won three WNBA championships. During the Valkyries' semifinal series sweep, Stokes used her experience to make things tough for Wilson and the Aces. Now she will try to do the same against Reese and the Dream. -- Voepel

9. DeWanna Bonner, Atlanta Dream
Forward | 6-foot-4

Playoff stats: 13.2 PPG, 6.4 RPG, 1.6 APG

After starting the season in Phoenix, Bonner joined the Dream with five games left in the regular season and has been a seamless fit so far for Atlanta, which desperately needed more depth entering the postseason. The two-time WNBA champion has slotted into the starting five since Gray went down with her injury and has hit double figures in four of Atlanta's five playoff games, including a 23-point outing in Game 1 of the semifinals. -- Philippou

10. Kayla Thornton, Golden State Valkyries
Forward | 6-foot-1

Playoff stats: 10.8 PPG, 5.7 RPG, 0.5 APG

Known for her 3-point shooting and perimeter defense abilities, Thornton has raised her game in the postseason. She's averaging more than three points more per game than the regular season and her 3-point percentage has climbed from 34.7% to 42.3%. This is the most productive the 11-year veteran has ever been in the postseason, scoring 16 points with three triples in Game 2 against the Aces and putting up 18 points and nine rebounds in the Game 3 closeout to advance to the Finals. Those points were the second- and third-most of her playoff career. Four of Thornton's five double-digit playoff scoring games have come in 2026. -- Copeland

11. Cecilia Zandalasini, Golden State Valkyries
Forward | 6-foot-2

Playoff stats: 8.5 PPG, 2.2 RPG, 1.2 SPG

Zandalasini's performance in Game 1 of the first round against the Wings illustrates how important she is for Golden State and how dangerous she can be as a floor spacer. She scored 22 points in that game, knocking down 4 of 5 3-point attempts. This is what she does best: hit important shots and provide momentum-shifting stretches. She is shooting 42.1% from beyond the arc in the postseason, while also playing an important role as a rebounder. -- Andrews

12. Naz Hillmon, Atlanta Dream
Forward | 6-foot-2

Playoff stats: 5.2 PPG, 4.4 RPG, 2.6 APG

Hillmon's scoring might be a bit down from her regular-season numbers (9.1 PPG) but she has still made an impact for the Dream in the playoffs -- especially defensively, where she made life difficult for Breanna Stewart in the semifinals. -- Philippou

13. Kaila Charles, Golden State Valkyries
Guard/forward | 6-foot-1

Playoff stats: 6.3 PPG, 4.2 RPG, 0.8 APG

Golden State is the fifth WNBA team Charles -- a second-round draft pick in 2020 -- has played for, and it has been the best fit for her. Charles has played in every game this season, and her stats are almost identical between the regular season and postseason. She personifies the team chemistry and willingness to play however many minutes she is given with the same energy. It's part of what has made her a fan favorite in the Bay Area. -- Voepel

14. Kaitlyn Chen, Golden State Valkyries
Guard | 5-foot-9

Playoff stats: 6.0 PPG, 1.5 RPG, 1.2 APG

Chen's minutes have dipped in the playoffs, but she has made the most of limited opportunities. Getting 17 minutes in Game 1 against the Wings, she scored eight points with two rebounds, two assists and two 3-pointers. In Game 1 against the Aces, Chen scored a playoff career-high 11 points in 22 minutes, also grabbing three rebounds. Starring in her reserve role, the second-year guard has been the loudest and most animated supporter of her teammates while on the bench. -- Copeland

15. Isobel Borlase, Atlanta Dream
Guard | 5-foot-11

Playoff stats: 5.6 PPG, 1.8 RPG, 0.8 APG

The Dream drafted "Izzy" in the second round in 2024 out of Australia at age 19, knowing she would need some time to develop before joining the WNBA. Atlanta's plans for her have worked out. The rookie, who turned 22 in September, appeared in all 44 games in the regular season, averaging 4.8 points and 13.0 minutes. In the postseason, she has played a similar role, giving the Dream important minutes off the bench, especially with fellow guard Gray having sat out most of the semifinals. -- Voepel

stories.headline: F1 2027 driver lineups: Who has a seat - and who's out of contract?
stories.summary: The 2026 rule changes threw Formula 1 into a new era of challenges and uncertainty, but the real moments of unpredictability are still to come.
stories.body:
The 2026 rule changes threw Formula 1 into a new era of challenges and uncertainty, but the real moments of unpredictability are still to come.

Most drivers secured short-term deals to survive the regulation shift, leaving the grid wide open for the following year. With only a handful of drivers locked into long-term contracts almost every seat on the grid is up for grabs.

Here is our early look at what the future holds for the current Formula 1 lineup.

McLaren

Lando Norris - 'multi-year deal' beyond 2030

Prior to the start of the 2024 F1 season Norris agreed to an "extended multi-year contract beyond 2025."

The reigning champion has now signed a new contract with McLaren until at least 2030. The deal, which includes one of his title-winning Formula 1 cars as a gift from the team, also has the option of a "multi-year" extension beyond 2030.

Oscar Piastri - 'multi-year deal' beyond 2026

Ahead of the first race of the 2025 F1 season Piastri also signed a multi-year contract extension. His previous deal already ran until the end of 2026, and his latest agreement is likely to keep him at McLaren until at least the end of 2028 -- though speculation continues to rumble on about his long-term future.

Ferrari

Lewis Hamilton - 2027

While an exact end date of Hamilton's contract -- signed after completing one of the biggest driver moves in F1 history -- was never officially communicated, Hamilton admitted earlier this year that he still had a contract in place for 2027. That means he got at least a three-year deal at Ferrari, something he had also been seeking at Mercedes.

Amid retirement rumours, Hamilton has also crushed speculation and assured fans that he wasn't going anywhere just yet.

He said: "There's a lot of people that are trying to retire me, and that's not even in my thoughts. I'm already thinking of what will be next, and planning for, like, the next five years. But I still plan to be here for some time."

Charles Leclerc - 2028

Leclerc, who first joined Ferrari in 2019, signed another multi-year extension ahead of the 2026 Monaco Grand Prix.

The team did not publicly reveal an exact expiry date, but the new agreement is understood to take Leclerc to 2028 and potentially beyond, giving Ferrari long-term security over one side of its driver lineup.

Red Bull

Max Verstappen - 2030

Red Bull confirmed in 2022 that four-time world champion Verstappen would remain with the team until the end of 2028 in one of the longest deals on the F1 grid.

Sources told ESPN that performance-related clauses in Verstappen's contract could allow him to leave early, but the Dutchman has now signed a new contract extension with Red Bull until 2030 ahead of the Dutch Grand Prix.

Isack Hadjar - 2027

Isack Hadjar was promoted from Racing Bulls to partner Verstappen for the 2026 season after an impressive rookie campaign. He has now signed a contract extension with Red Bull, securing his seat for the 2027 season.

Mercedes

George Russell - beyond 2026

Russell agreed a new deal with Mercedes ahead of the 2026 season following lengthy negotiations with team principal Toto Wolff.

Although the agreement was initially confirmed as taking him through at least 2026, Russell has since described it as a multi-year deal and said he will fulfill the performance clauses in his contract to stay at Mercedes next year.

Kimi Antonelli - TBC

Mercedes' Antonelli has only been given one-year contracts since his debut, but given his form this season there's no way he'll be leaving the Silver Arrows. Right?

No official announcements have been made yet, but Antonelli could be celebrating both a maiden title and a bumper new deal this year.

Aston Martin

Fernando Alonso - TBC

Alonso's current Aston Martin deal runs until the end of the 2026 season, and he said a decision on his future will come later in the year. At 45 years old, the decision is likely to be between continuing with an underperforming Aston Martin team, or calling time on his F1 career once and for all.

Lance Stroll - TBC

Stroll signed a contract extension in 2024 which kept him with Aston Martin for 2025 "and beyond," but no specific end date was announced. Part of that ambiguity, of course, is because he's the son of team owner Lawrence Stroll.

He remains with the team for 2026, although his position for 2027 has not formally been confirmed.

Alpine

Pierre Gasly - 2028

Gasly is one of the drivers whose future is already settled -- the Frenchman signed a new multi-year agreement with Alpine in 2025 which keeps him locked in at the team until at least the end of the 2028 season.

Franco Colapinto - 2027

Colapinto retained his Alpine seat alongside Gasly for 2026 after taking over from Jack Doohan during the previous season. He has now signed a new contract with the team, meaning the Argentinian will continue with Alpine for the 2027 season.

Haas

Rafael Câmara - 'multi-year deal' beyond 2027

F2 star Câmara will replace Esteban Ocon for the 2027 season on a multi-year agreement. The reigning Formula 3 champion and current Formula 2 leader will make his debut in F1 and will partner fellow Ferrari Driver Academy member Oliver Bearman.

Oliver Bearman - TBC

Bearman joined Haas on a multi-year deal when he became a full-time F1 driver in 2025. The exact duration of Bearman's contract has not been made public, leaving his 2027 status uncertain for now.

However, sources with good knowledge of the team's thinking have told ESPN that Bearman is almost certain to stay with the team in 2027 unless a Ferrari seat opens up, then the Englishman remains effectively loaned to Haas.

Racing Bulls

Liam Lawson - TBC

Lawson remained with Racing Bulls for 2026 after rebuilding his season following a short-lived promotion to Red Bull the previous year.

His seat is only confirmed for the current season, meaning the New Zealander will again have to prove his case if he is to stay within the Red Bull set-up in 2027.

Arvid Lindblad - TBC

Lindblad became the latest Red Bull junior to make the jump to Formula 1 when he was handed a Racing Bulls seat for 2026.

The rookie is currently only confirmed for this season and the team have played down speculation over their driver lineup for 2027. You'd be shocked to see him go anywhere, though.

Williams

Carlos Sainz - 'multi-year deal' beyond 2026

Sainz originally joined Williams on a deal covering the 2025 and 2026 seasons, with "options to extend" his stay beyond that. He has recently spoken about wanting to make the Williams project work, leading to him signing a new multi-year extension with the team.

Alex Albon - 2027

Albon signed a new one-year contract with Williams during the summer break, tying him down for the 2027 season. The short-term deal is interesting, given Albon's last contract -- signed in 2024 -- was for multiple years. Keeping those options open?

Audi

Nico Hulkenberg - TBC

Hulkenberg joined Sauber ahead of its transformation into the Audi team on a multi-year contract in 2025.

There are believed to be options in his deal which could allow him to remain with Audi beyond 2026, but an exact end date has not been announced.

Gabriel Bortoleto - TBC

Bortoleto joined Hulkenberg at Sauber before the team's transition to Audi and also signed a multi-year deal.

The Brazilian is contracted through at least the end of 2026, but his place for 2027 has not yet been officially confirmed.

Cadillac

Sergio Perez - 2027

Perez returned to the Formula 1 grid with Cadillac for the team's debut season in 2026 after spending a year away from racing.

The Mexican joined on a multi-year agreement understood to be on similar terms to teammate Valtteri Bottas, putting him in line to remain with Cadillac for 2027.

Valtteri Bottas - 2027

Bottas also returned to a full-time race seat with Cadillac after spending 2025 as Mercedes' reserve driver.

The Finn signed a multi-year deal which runs until at least the end of 2027, giving the new team one of the few already settled driver pairings heading into next season.

stories.headline: UFC champ Alexander Volkanovski proposes 'send-off' superbout vs. Justin Gaethje
stories.summary: UFC featherweight champion Alexander Volkanovski is calling for a "send-off" superfight against lightweight champion Justin Gaethje.
stories.body:
UFC featherweight champion Alexander Volkanovski has proposed a "send-off" superfight between himself and lightweight champion Justin Gaethje.

Volkanovski (28-4) is scheduled to defend his 145-pound title against Movsar Evloev (20-0) at UFC 333 on Oct. 24 in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates. Arguably the greatest featherweight of all time, Volkanovski has acknowledged he is approaching the end of his career at 38 years old. Gaethje, 37, has acknowledged the same since he claimed the UFC's 155-pound title for the first time in June.

With both champions seemingly near the end of their time in the Octagon, Volkanovski has suggested a winner-take-all scenario in 2027.

"Imagine that, do it as a send-off," Volkanovski told the "Who Da Fook Are These Guys?" podcast. "Gaethje, Volk. I think he's said that he maybe has one more. That could be a superfight. Let's do a superfight with the lightweight title on the line. We can both see everyone off with a crazy superfight. That could be really good."

Volkanovski, of Australia, has already tried to capture the lightweight title. He famously challenged then-lightweight champion Islam Makhachev twice in a 10-month span in 2023. He suffered a razor-close decision loss to Makhachev in their first meeting in February then lost by first-round knockout in an October rematch that was scheduled on short notice.

Gaethje (28-5) has not even guaranteed whether he will fight again or retire off his historic win at the White House in June, but he has stated that he believes his next challenger would be lightweight contender Arman Tsarukyan. Volkanovski appears to be throwing his name into the mix in the hope of changing those plans.

"He's said, 'What's the point of doing rematches,'" Volkanovski said. "Let's do a superfight then [retire] straight away after, let the divisions sort themselves out. The UFC would be happy for that. Let's make it happen."

stories.headline: Judge sides with NRL over NZ Rugby on Chiefs name
stories.summary: Rugby league has struck the first blow in the Chief name wars, with New Zealand Rugby's urgent injunction denied ahead of the new PNG NRL club's jersey reveal.
stories.body:
New Zealand's High Court has knocked back an application for an interim injunction on the PNG Chiefs NRL franchise using its name in the country.

New Zealand Rugby (NZR) had rushed to court ahead of the PNG team's logo and jersey reveal in Port Moresby next week.

The organisation claimed use of the Chiefs name, also the name of the long-standing Super Rugby Pacific outfit, would cause confusion and damage to the brand value.

But a judge at Friday's two-hour Wellington hearing turned down the application after hearing an injunction could harm the NRL expansion outfit's efforts to attract players ahead of a 2028 debut.

The dispute remains though, with the application for a final injunction still before the court and legal action in Australia a consideration.

ARLC executive chairman Peter V'landys last week labelled NZR's action one of "mind-blowing hypocrisy", using the example of the Auckland Blues' arrival decades after the NSW Blues "had been the Blues".

"Today's decision is not a judgement on the strength of our case, and the matter will still be heard in full," NZR boss Steve Lancaster said.

"As the trademark holder, our responsibility to protect the Chiefs brand hasn't changed. We remain open to working with the ARLC on a solution."

NZR's lawyer Earl Gray argued on Friday that the PNG Chiefs' use of 'PNG Chiefs' and 'Chiefs' interchangeably created confusion for fans of both codes and that, with no clear distinction between the two, it would strip the rugby Chiefs' brand exclusivity.

He said NZR had trademark protections for the Chiefs in New Zealand that the NRL had not acknowledged.

ARLC laywer Clive Elliot argued that the request for an urgent injunction, about a year after NZR became aware of the PNG Chiefs name, was not appropriate.

He said an injunction now would cloud the franchise's reputation ahead of a recruitment blitz once free agency opens in November.

stories.summary: Our experts dive into the odds and player props for Week 6 and offer their betting tips and favorite plays.

Value is value, no matter where -- or how -- you find it. And that's what we'll aim to do each week in this space: find betting value.

Ben Solak, Seth Walder and Matt Bowen bring different perspectives into how they approach sports betting. Solak leans on his expertise in player evaluation and the X's and O's to find edges, while Walder relies on statistical models to pick out plus-expected value bets, focusing mainly on defense. It's a tough week to pick games. However, we are going to make some plays here, starting with my picks for the Texans and Jaguars in London. Here's how I see Sunday's matchup playing out ...

When the Texans have the ball: Quarterback C.J. Stroud has played really good football over the past two games, coinciding with Nico Collins' return from a hamstring injury. Yes, Coen and the Jaguars will work to create run-pass balance, but this game comes down to Lawrence's ability to make plays on third downs.

Solak's plays

C.J. Stroud passing yards OVER 257.5 (-111)

The Jacksonville Jaguars have a generally strong defense, but it has some vulnerabilities. They're second in points per drive allowed and third in EPA per play allowed -- but dead last in explosive pass rate allowed, with 17.2% of the pass attempts against them going for at least a 16-yard gain. Specifically, throws to the intermediate area of the field have been easily accessible. Guess what the entire Texans passing attack is built around? Stroud has thrown an in-breaker on 41.1% of his pass attempts this season (fifth-highest rate) and has thrown intermediate on 26% of his dropbacks (seventh most). You see where my head is at with this one.

I think there are two ways to get into this angle here: Stroud passing yards and Nico Collins receiving yards. Collins has five straight games of 100-plus receiving yards against the Jaguars and is looking to tie the NFL record for consecutive games of 100-plus yards against the same opponent. I expect a heavy diet of Collins, given his strength at these specific vulnerabilities.

I will lean to Stroud for the potential of big explosives to Kayshon Boutte, Jaylin Noel or the newly acquired Marvin Harrison Jr. I'll be on Collins receiving overs and Stroud passing overs when building out my bet card this week.

The Los Angeles Rams are 12.5-point favorites against the Arizona Cardinals this week. They ran the ball with impunity against Arizona last season. Running backs had 253 yards on 33 carries in the Rams' Week 14 win and 119 on 25 carries in a Week 18 win. That kept Stafford from totaling big days through the air. The Bills have allowed only 3.7 yards per carry to running backs this season, the seventh-lowest figure through five weeks; the Cardinals, at 4.2 allowed, are more around league average. With OL Alaric Jackson suspended, the Rams seem less likely to pass it and risk big hits on Stafford in what should be a quiet divisional win.

The Rams have generally been in competitive contests all year. In three of their past four games, all of which saw Stafford clear 300 total passing yards, the Rams have needed to cover second-half deficits. That's much less likely here, and I'll take the under on Stafford accordingly.

Aaron Rodgers 2+ passing touchdowns (+137)

I love taking Rodgers passing touchdown props because of how aggressively his teams tend to throw the ball in the red zone. The Pittsburgh Steelers lead the league in called red zone pass rate at 76%. Inside the 10-yard line, that leaps to 81%. Rodgers has thrown three touchdown passes in each of the past three contests, though those have largely been explosive passes with big YAC rather than short-area tosses.

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers' passing defense has surrendered only seven passing touchdowns, but the Bucs have a particularly bad matchup on the Steelers in the passing game, given how poorly their linebackers play in coverage. Receiving back Jaylen Warren, who is on a career-best pace for overall yardage, should win in space against Alex Anzalone and Josiah Trotter. Similarly, with safety Antoine Winfield Jr. expected to miss another game, the Bucs' safety position can be attacked by tight ends Darnell Washington and Pat Freiermuth, who are Rodgers' preferred red zone targets anyway.

Rodgers is only two behind Peyton Manning on the list for career passing touchdowns, and you can bet he knows it, too. I think we see a pass-happy approach in the red zone from Rodgers.

Tanner McKee 19+ completions (-101)

The Philadelphia Eagles are as decimated of an offense as we've seen in the league this season. Three starting linemen from Week 1 are out for this game, as are RB1 Saquon Barkley, WR1 DeVonta Smith and now QB1 Jalen Hurts, who has a blood clot that might keep him out indefinitely. In for Hurts and contending with this depleted roster is backup Tanner McKee, who originally lost the QB2 job out of camp to Andy Dalton.

But McKee isn't a slouch. In two career starts, McKee has 30 and 24 completions. He's a rhythm pocket passer who knows where to go with the football. The Carolina Panthers have been a stiff pass defense for much of this season by completion percentage, but they're still down both starting cornerbacks in Mike Jackson and Jaycee Horn, and we've seen the backups play for only one game in Week 4 before Carolina's Week 5 bye. It's still unclear how good Carolina's secondary will be in the interim.

As such, I'm betting on McKee, in what is likely a trailing game script, to take underneath completions, especially with the running back injuries behind Barkley, which should discourage the Eagles from too many handoffs. I'll be taking alts on completions here up to 24+.

Brock Bowers 8+ receptions (+140)

Bowers has seen 14, 11 and 10 targets through three healthy games this season as he continues to establish himself as one of the league's best receivers. And that's what he is; 83% of Bowers' routes have come from the slot or wide alignments this season, and his primary matchup defender in each of his three games has been a cornerback. Bowers gets thrown to, and treated like, a wideout.

No defense has seen a greater volume of plays go to receivers lined up out wide than the Bills, because of both their weaker cornerback room and the leads they generate on offense, forcing opponents into heavy pass scripts. Buffalo has seen 85 pass attempts and 55 completions to outside receivers (both lead the league), and its passer rating allowed to quarterbacks targeting outside receivers is eighth worst among league defenses. You can throw on the Bills everywhere, but especially to the outside.

As such, I expect easy volume for Bowers, especially as the Las Vegas Raiders lack the necessary running game to shorten the contest against a high-flying Bills offense. With plenty of snaps and a desire to get the ball out of Kirk Cousins' hands quickly, receptions is my preferred angle over receiving yards here.

The England international picked up a calf injury in last weekend's defeat at Crystal Palace and has not trained all week.
